items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

ctx.x: Has — this is sort of an obvious question but paying your rent as a musician, making a living, has there been ups and downs for you?

Sure. But never to the point of, you know, red alert. Never to that point. It always worked out. You know like after Rod left and I started the new Dry Jack thing, you know there was some financial struggles but like for instance right after that band broke up I moved into an apartment down near Woodstock and my landlord was Dave Holland.

items.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023
items.q: he was one of the most, he was one of the kindest most gentle spirit... we’d listen to it and talk about it and analyze... You know he taught me so much stuff.

ctx.x: Oh the man, oh just — he was one of the most, he was one of the kindest most gentle spirit. He was like a kid in a lot of ways. And you know we’d listen to music. I remember this one day he got out you know like four or five CDs from different people. He was always getting CDs. And we’d listen to it and talk about it and analyze, and he’d be talking about you know when he went to the Pacific, you know in college when he was a young man. And he’s going, “I could play like Art Tatum, man, I had that accident.…
